_meta.indication: Indicated to decrease the incidence of infection, as manifested by febrile neutropenia, in adult patients with non-myeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive anti-cancer drugs associated with a clinically significant incidence of febrile neutropenia

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority study of four 21-day cycles of a single fixed dose (20 mg) of F-627
pivotal_trials.population: Females with Stage II-IV breast cancer receiving docetaxel and doxorubicin (TA) chemotherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Duration of severe neutropenia in cycle 1 of chemotherapy
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean duration of severe neutropenia in cycle 1 was 1.4 days for F-627 vs 4.3 days for placebo (superiority); febrile neutropenia in cycle 1 was 4.8% (F-627) vs 25.6% (placebo)

nct_ctgov.title: Placebo-controlled Trial of F-627 in Women With Breast Cancer Receiving Myelotoxic Chemotherapy

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, open-label, active-controlled (pegfilgrastim/Neulasta) noninferiority study of four 21-day cycles
pivotal_trials.population: Females with Stage I-III breast cancer receiving docetaxel and cyclophosphamide (TC) chemotherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Duration of severe neutropenia in cycle 1 of chemotherapy
pivotal_trials.result: Mean duration of severe neutropenia in cycle 1 was 0.2 days for both F-627 and Neulasta; mean difference 0.0 days (95% CI -0.1, 0.1), meeting noninferiority (margin 0.6 days)

nct_ctgov.title: Neulasta-controlled Trial of F-627 in Women With Breast Cancer Receiving Myelotoxic Chemotherapy

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were nausea (51%), anemia (15%), and thrombocytopenia (12%); class-associated serious risks include splenic rupture, ARDS, serious allergic reactions/anaphylaxis, sickle cell crisis, glomerulonephritis, leukocytosis, and capillary leak syndrome
target_moa: A recombinant human G-CSF receptor agonist (Fc-fusion protein) that binds to G-CSF receptors on hematopoietic cells and stimulates proliferation, differentiation, and end-cell functional activation of neutrophils
modality: Recombinant Fc-fusion protein (human G-CSF linked to a human IgG2 Fc fragment); other

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee was convened because there were no safety or efficacy issues requiring one

basis.text: Application reviewed under standard (not priority) review

summary.text: BLA 761134 was submitted by Evive Biotechnology and reviewed under standard review; efficacy was established in two adequate and well-controlled trials (GC-627-04 vs placebo and GC-627-05 vs pegfilgrastim). It was a traditional (full) approval with no expedited designations, and was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: Evive Biotechnology Singapore Pte. Ltd submitted a biologics license application (BLA) 761134 for Ryzneuta (efbemalenograstim alfa-vuxw, F-627), a granulocyte colony stimulating factor (G-CSF).

Priority or standard	Standard
Submit date(s)	3/30/2021
Substantial evidence of effectiveness was established in two main trials, GC-627-04 and GC-627-05.

Your application for efbemalenogastim alfa-vuxw was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for a biologic of this class.

requirement.text: 4530-1 Conduct a multicenter, open-label, study to assess the safety, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of efbemalenogastim alfa in at least 40 pediatric patients 1 month to <17 years of age with non-myeloid solid tumors or lymphomas receiving myelosuppressive anti-cancer drugs associated with a clinically significant incidence of febrile neutropenia.

requirement.text: 4530-2 Submit pediatric assessments for Ryzneuta (efbemalenograstim alfa) as described in section 505B(a)(2)(A) of the FD&C Act, including development of an "appropriate formulation" (presentation) that can be used to directly and accurately administer Ryzneuta (efbemalenograstim alpha) to pediatric patients (1 month to <17 years of age). Conduct any necessary human factors studies to evaluate the ability of healthcare providers and caregivers to measure the appropriate doses.
